evidence.description: The first execution's preflight record (records/preflight-2026-11-28.md, PR #814, merge 63408e1c), which closed Spec 112 as filed under kill criterion KC-1 with the three failure mechanisms measured; the revision registration (records/revision-registration-2026-11-28.md) answering those mechanisms; and the program's kill-criterion discipline as filed in Specs 109, 110, and 112.

falsification_tests: A leg of the revision executed under a design other than the revision registration; a floor, threshold, or parameter of the revised design adjusted after the revision freeze; the whole-form class or a one-segment candidate present in the frozen harness's scoring; a paradigm, anchor, or threshold taken from the comparison side (the Class B template or the gold morphology) rather than induced under the registered rules.
claims.text: The revision of Spec 112 is the design its revision registration specifies: a segmenter with no whole-form class, an inventory of substrings recurring in at least 2 distinct host forms plus every single character, candidate segmentations of two or more segments, and all other segmentation parameters carried from the first freeze; a sequence-anchored slot grammar (induced invocation frame, induced offering anchor and family, filiation paradigms induced as marker strings under registered host, occurrence, zone, and initial-share floors, slot order induced by precedence majorities, parse by anchor zones); and partial proposals as the revised segmenter's final segments under a threshold re-derived on the development partition from a character-shuffled null; and no leg of the revision runs under any other design. Does not establish: that the revised design is correct, that it will pass the preflight, or that any structure it induces is a fact about the Meroitic language rather than a candidate about the corpus.

evidence.description: The first execution's preflight record (records/preflight-2026-11-28.md, PR #814, merge 63408e1c), which closed Spec 112 as filed under kill criterion KC-1 with the three failure mechanisms measured; the revision registration (records/revision-registration-2026-11-28.md) answering those mechanisms; and the program's kill-criterion discipline as filed in Specs 109, 110, and 112.

falsification_tests: A corpus output of the revision filed without a preflight pass in full on the record; a preflight figure accepted without the independent recomputation; a floor, ground-truth set, or scoring rule differing in any particular from the first execution's; the preflight run before the fixture proofs passed.
claims.text: The revision's conformance preflight gates the revision's corpus output exactly as the first execution's preflight gated its own: the same floors (P-1 median boundary F1 at least 0.80; P-2 slot-sequence match at least 90 percent of the labeled texts with the presentation slot highest-variance; P-3 partial precision at least 0.80 with shuffle yield at most 20 percent of the real yield), the same ground-truth sets byte-identical to the filed sets, and the same scoring rules, with the preflight figures judged by an independent recomputation from the filed outputs, and the fixture proofs of the revision registration as a precondition that runs before the preflight. Does not establish: that passing the preflight would validate the design's outputs as readings, or that the floors are the right floors; they are the first registration's floors, carried unchanged by the kill-criterion discipline.

evidence.description: The first execution's preflight record (records/preflight-2026-11-28.md, PR #814, merge 63408e1c), which closed Spec 112 as filed under kill criterion KC-1 with the three failure mechanisms measured; the revision registration (records/revision-registration-2026-11-28.md) answering those mechanisms; and the program's kill-criterion discipline as filed in Specs 109, 110, and 112.

falsification_tests: The revision continuing past a failed preflight leg or a failed fixture proof; a second revision executed under this registration; an induction output of the revision presented as a reading, a morpheme identification, or a translation.
claims.text: The revision's outcome, whatever it is, is filed as the outcome: a preflight pass in full licenses the revision's corpus induction (ranked candidates with margins and full generation provenance, no meanings assigned) and nothing else; a failure of any leg closes the revision as filed under the carried kill criteria, and a further revision of the search design is a new commission outside this registration, never a continuation of it. Does not establish: that a passed revision would constitute a decipherment result, or that a failed revision falsifies structure induction for Meroitic in general; either outcome is a finding about this design at this corpus.

falsification_tests: An output of the revision entered as an input to Spec 102's vocabulary, gates, or scoring, or to Spec 109 Stage 5, without a new registration deciding that use on its own record; a write by the revision into either spec's tree; a gloss or meaning assigned to a Meroitic form anywhere in the revision's records.
claims.text: The revision is corpus-internal structure only, under the same non-interference as the first registration: it writes nothing into Spec 102's or Spec 109's trees, changes no gate, source rule, or pin of either, supplies no vocabulary to Spec 102, leaves Spec 109 Stage 5 gated on Spec 102 exactly as registered, and assigns no gloss or meaning to any Meroitic form. Does not establish: that the revision's structures could never legitimately inform those studies; only that any such use is a separate, registered decision, not a consequence of this one.
